finding.claim: Expired tokens are accepted from the verifier cache when the token has exp but no numeric iat, for up to cacheTTL (default 600000 ms) after exp.
finding.source: Attacker holds a token that was valid when first presented; caching enabled; token signed without iat (e.g. signer noTimestamp: true, signer.js:96).
finding.sink: Cache hit returns payload without re-running the exp validator (verifier.js:377).

trace.note: hasIat is false when iat is absent, so the exp branch is skipped
maxTTL = now + cacheTTL is used because cacheValue[2] is still 0
cache.get hit on a later verify of the same token
now <= max holds within cacheTTL after exp

finding.guards_checked: Only successful verifications are cached (verifier.js:426). cacheTTL cap applied (verifier.js:133-134). exp honored only when iat is numeric (verifier.js:125). Nothing re-checks exp on a cache hit. Caching is opt-in (verifier.js:606).

finding.claim: A Buffer token throws an uncaught TypeError when caching is enabled, because hashToken calls token.split on the raw token before decoding.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled token passed as a Buffer (e.g. raw request body) to a verifier with caching enabled.
finding.sink: cacheKeyBuilder(token) -> hashToken -> token.split (utils.js:46), thrown synchronously before the decode try-block (verifier.js:386).

trace.note: Buffer tokens are accepted by the type check
cache branch entered when cache is enabled
token.split is not a function on Buffer, so TypeError is thrown

finding.guards_checked: Type check at verifier.js:353-360 only rejects non-string, non-Buffer input. Caching is off by default (verifier.js:84-85).

finding.claim: Non-canonical base64url signature segments are accepted, so one valid signature has several distinct token strings. String-keyed revocation or replay checks can be bypassed. Not a forgery. Unverified by execution.
finding.source: Attacker holds one valid token and can alter the unused trailing bits of its last signature character.
finding.sink: Application revocation, single-use or replay check keyed on the raw token string; verifier cache keyed on the raw token string (verifier.js:364).

trace.note: signature segment passes alphabet check with non-canonical trailing bits
timingSafeEqual compares decoded bytes, so all variants verify

finding.guards_checked: Alphabet check only. Header and payload are not malleable because the signature covers their exact text. Only the signature segment is affected. The claim that Node ignores the unused bits is from code reading and needs a test to confirm.

finding.claim: maxAge is silently not enforced for tokens without iat, because absent claims are skipped by the validator loop, so the check fails open.
finding.source: Issuer omits iat (e.g. noTimestamp: true); attacker cannot add iat to a signed token.
finding.sink: maxAge validator on iat is skipped.

trace.note: absent claim causes the validator to be skipped
maxAge validator is registered on iat

finding.guards_checked: Signature verified before claims. Without iat the maxAge check is a no-op. Configuration-dependent.

finding.claim: The signer header option is spread last, so it can override alg and typ. Only dangerous if the application passes request-derived data as the header option. Informational.
finding.source: Application passes untrusted data as the header option (developer-dependent).
finding.sink: Emitted token header alg differs from the algorithm used to sign.

trace.note: header object built with alg, typ, kid
...additionalHeader spread last, overriding alg and typ

finding.guards_checked: header is type-checked only as an object (signer.js:296-298). No verifier path found that accepts the mismatch.
